liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Drums** (2 reviews): A percussion jam segues into a jam resembling the disco-era Stayin' Alive; Reviewer found the Drums segment less than good [8][18]
- **Jam** (1 review, 1 other source): The Jerry and Keith jam is groovy and reminded the reviewer of Diana Ross's Upside Down; The jam includes a Stayin' Alive tease [2][18]
- **The Music Never Stopped** (1 review): Jam starts around 3:20 at a slightly slow tempo, a meander, with an abrupt turn near 5:20 [12]
- **Stella Blue** (1 review): The jam into Stella Blue follows a strong Drums with an involved crowd; choosing Stella over Truckin' seemed peculiar [13]
- **Playing In The Band** (1 review): The second-set Playin' jam is described as floating on clouds [8]
- **Werewolves Of London** (1 review): Reviewer never heard the Dead play it before or after, and wondered if they'd imagined it [10]

## Setlist highlights

- **Werewolves Of London**: rare: 12 archived performances [20]

## The recordings

- **gd1978-04-21.sbd.miller.97501.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 20 songs; 160 min; rated 4.18/5 by 11 [1]
- **gd1978-04-21.123212.sbd.miller.flac16**: soundboard; 20 songs; 163 min; rated 4.25/5 by 4 [2]
- **gd78-04-21.sbd.cotsman.10149.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 20 songs; 160 min; rated 3.87/5 by 15 [3]. Said about its sound: Recording sounds muddy, less crisp than others from this tour; Reviewer finds the sound quality good on headphones; Some issues with sound levels and quality, but overall very listenable [11][12][13]
- **gd1978-04-21.165007.aud.gale.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 21 songs; 160 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [4]. Said about its sound: Start of Promised Land is clipped; first complete audience source in general circulation [4]
- **gd1978-04-21.151824.1p.2.shure.sm57.sublette.mattes.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 14 songs; 131 min [6]. Said about its sound: Brown Eyed Women's start and Music Never Stopped's end are clipped; two cuts in Stella Blue [6]

## Around the show

- Early in set two, Bobby banters about Jerry's craving for cigarettes [8]
- Reviewer from Lexington says only a few thousand fans sat in the roughly 24,000-capacity arena [9]
- Reviewer says this was the Dead's first Lexington show and also their last [9]
- Bobby and Phil invited the crowd to move closer, making the show feel unusually intimate [10]
- Reviewer wonders who failed to promote the show, since the Dead usually filled arenas [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1978-04-21.sbd.miller.97501.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master -> Dat (44.1k) [1]
- **gd1978-04-21.123212.sbd.miller.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master -> Dat (44.1k) [2]. Also: Patched version of shnid 97501, made from DATs lent by Rob Eaton; Matt Smith supplied the patch source; Joe B. Jones helped correct it [2]
- **gd78-04-21.sbd.cotsman.10149.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [3]
- **gd1978-04-21.165007.aud.gale.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Unknown; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Low Gen audience recording; Unknown equipment, from the Dan Gale collection [4]. Also: A Shure SM57 source from Kathy Sublette supplies a 0:42 patch in the Jam before Stella Blue [4]
- **gd1978-04-21.151824.1p.2.shure.sm57.sublette.mattes.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Kathy Sublette; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Kathy Sublette's Master Audience Cassettes; Shure SM57 mics > Sony-TC158 [6]

## Art and photos

- Poster by LiveGRATEFUL.net: [Grateful Dead 1978-04-21 Fri Rupp Arena, University of Kentucky, Lexington, KY](https://www.livegrateful.net/post/1367839340717/grateful-dead-1978-04-21-fri-rupp-arena) [21]
